task_summary: Implemented two new authenticated product-catalog internal API endpoints: POST /api/internal/catalog/source-imports/batch (GigaB2B source import with variant creation, commercial upsert, run/row tracking, and replay idempotency) and POST /api/internal/catalog/listing-candidates/query (read-only batch query returning canonical product data with Mercari shop1-shop4 mappings). Added 67 new tests (136 total, all passing). Both typecheck and test suites pass cleanly.
scope_statement: Added handler functions, types, Page routes, tests, tsconfig entries, and documentation for source-imports/batch and listing-candidates/query endpoints. No credentials, databases, network calls, or production access used. No migrations created. Reused existing catalog authentication and PostgREST helpers.
commands_or_checks_run: npm run test:internal-api (136 tests, 136 pass, 0 fail)
findings: Existing handler pattern uses DI via fetchFn parameter for mock testing
PostgREST helpers (supabaseRows, postgrestWrite) already support batched reads/writes with merge-duplicates
No pipeline_lock table exists; run resolution uses read-before-write by source_system + file_hash
Listing-candidates handler needed array-based shop map to detect multiple listings per shop conflict
product_variants.sku is the unique key for variant upserts; item_code has a partial unique index
product_commercials uses variant_id as primary key for upserts
risks: source_import_runs has no unique constraint on (source_system, file_hash) — read-before-write could race if pipelined lock is absent
Run finalization PATCH failure is logged but not returned as error to caller — partial success possible if PATCH fails after row/commercial upserts succeed
